comments.comment: To clarify he said, “I never let one asset class get over 20% of my net worth” 11:28. This is important to understand because even if you go into different sectors in the stock market you are still in the same asset class (Stocks). True diversification or at least what he’s referring to here means knowing all the asset classes, stocks, bonds, real estate, precious metals, cash and cash equivalents, art work, intellectual property, businesses etc. And dividing your net worth into these classes. Hope this helps

At 3:07 when Kevin was discussing how to start creating a credit history, i thought he was going to say something completely different. I read a Suze Orman tip once and did what she recommended for my two daughters and it worked perfectly. She said, if you have good credit pass it on to your kids by getting them a credit card issued under your account but just don't give it to them.  I did that and within 6 weeks my daughters credit score went up well over 770. She inherited my 20 years of history on that card for her credit score without ever seeing or using the card.
